title: Use anchor field for precise comment placement instead of substring matching
description:
Comments are currently placed at the first paragraph where the quoted text appears as a substring. The Google Drive API returns an `anchor` field on each comment that encodes the exact document position, but it is currently fetched and discarded.

This means a comment may appear under the wrong paragraph if its quoted text also appears earlier in the document.

The fix in #deduplication addressed repeated comments but did not resolve placement accuracy. A proper fix would parse the `anchor` field and use it to map comments to the correct content element.

title: Bug: MIME type detection parses raw URL, often wrong
description: image_handler.py:126-130 — MIME type is detected by splitting sourceUri on '.' and taking the last segment. If sourceUri is something like 'https://example.com/image?v=2.0', the 'extension' is '0', which fails the check, and everything defaults to image/png. Fix: parse the URL path properly with urllib.parse.urlparse before extracting extension. E.g.: from urllib.parse import urlparse; path = urlparse(source_uri).path; ext = path.rsplit('.', 1)[-1].lower() if '.' in path else ''

title: Setup CLAUDE.md and permissions
Bug: image dedup counter always equals total_images
description: cli.py:355-356 — image_cache is Dict[str, str] (hash→filename). When iterating .items(), was_dedup is always a filename string (truthy), so deduplicated always equals total_images. The cache only stores unique images (duplicates reuse existing entries), so there's no way to know the dedup count from the cache. Fix: either add a separate counter for dedup hits, or just remove the dedup reporting since 'Downloaded N images' is sufficient.

title: Replace deprecated datetime.utcnow()
description: gdrive_client.py:105 — datetime.utcnow() was deprecated in Python 3.12 and will be removed in a future version. Replace with: from datetime import datetime, timezone; datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat().replace('+00:00', 'Z'). The project targets >=3.10 so it works today but emits deprecation warnings on 3.12+.

title: Replace raw tuples with a TabData dataclass
description: Throughout the code, tabs are passed as (tab_id, tab_name, content, inline_objects) 4-tuples and output files as (output_path, tab_name, content, inline_objects) 4-tuples. This makes call sites like tabs[0][3] cryptic. A simple dataclass would improve readability: @dataclass class TabData: tab_id: str; name: str; content: list; inline_objects: dict — then tab.name instead of tabs[0][1].
